findings.title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the user has never visited the topic (no TopicUser row exists). The very next line (107) calls tu.notification_level on this potentially-nil value, which will raise NoMethodError. This will happen for any user who clicks an unsubscribe link for a topic they received a notification about but never actually opened.

findings.title: State-changing action on GET request is vulnerable to CSRF
findings.body: The unsubscribe action modifies the user's notification level (a state change) but is routed as a GET request (config/routes.rb line 440-441). GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF token mechanism. An attacker can trick a logged-in user into changing their notification level by embedding the unsubscribe URL in an tag, a link preview, or any other mechanism that causes the browser to issue a GET request. This should be a POST/PUT action.

findings.title: Missing authorization check for topic visibility
findings.body: The unsubscribe action creates a TopicView and proceeds without calling guardian.ensure_can_see! on the topic. Unlike the show action which rescues Discourse::InvalidAccess, this action does not verify the user has permission to see the topic. For private messages or secure-category topics, this could allow a user to interact with (and confirm the existence of) a topic they should not have access to.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires unsubscribe_url interpolation which may not always be provided
findings.body: The unsubscribe_link locale string now contains %{unsubscribe_url}. This string is rendered in Email::MessageBuilder#body (line 90) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. If any current or future caller sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without also providing unsubscribe_url in the opts, I18n will raise MissingInterpolationArgument and the email will fail to send. Currently only send_notification_email provides both, but this creates a fragile coupling.

findings.title: Typo in computed property name: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The property is named stopNotificiationsText (with 'ii' instead of 'io' in Notifications). While the template references the same misspelled name so it works, this makes the code harder to maintain and search for, and could cause confusion if someone tries to reference it by the correct spelling.

findings.title: Triple-mustache renders unescaped HTML including user-controlled topic title
findings.body: The template uses {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} which renders raw HTML without escaping. The value includes model.fancyTitle interpolated into the locale string. While Discourse's fancyTitle applies some server-side sanitization, using triple-mustache with user-generated content (topic titles) is risky. If fancyTitle ever contains unescaped user input (e.g., via a bug or a plugin), this becomes an XSS vector. Consider using a component or helper that explicitly escapes the title before inserting it into the HTML string.
